The test image shows a soybean plant pulled from the ground with a bleached/white stem and wilted brown-gray leaves still attached. This is a stem/whole plant presentation. Top candidates based on part index: White_Mold, Sudden_death_syndrome, Phytophthora, Fusarium, Charcoal_Rot, Brown_Stem_Rot.

Now I'll view one reference from each of 8 different classes:

**Analysis:**

Test image: A soybean plant pulled from the soil, showing a pale/bleached white stem and wilted brown-gray dead leaves still attached to the plant. The stem has a notably blanched/white appearance.

Key observations:
- Bleached/white stem (not brown or gray)
- Dead leaves remaining attached to the plant
- Plant has collapsed and died
- No obvious chocolate-brown discoloration (rules out Phytophthora)
- No charcoal-gray coloring (rules out Charcoal_Rot)
- No reddish-brown canker at soil line (rules out Rhizoctonia)

**White Mold** is the best match: the characteristic bleached white stem and dead leaves remaining attached are hallmark signs. The two White Mold reference images confirm this pattern — pale/bleached stems (with sclerotia in one case). The symptom description specifically mentions "stems become soft, watery, and bleached white" and "wilted dead leaves remaining attached."
